HDD Market History And Projections

Tom Coughlin
Contributor
Opinions expressed by Forbes Contributors are their own.
Enterprise Tech
  • Share to Facebook

This piece gives results from our last Digital Storage Technology Newsletter on recent history and current projections for the HDD, and other storage technology, market.  This follows up from previous statements in an earlier blog, COVID-19 HDD Industry Impact.  Note that changes in the reporting of the HDD manufacturers give much less detail on the shipment of various types of HDDs, so the breakout of HDD units is an estimate.

Total HDD shipments in CQ1 2020 were down 12.9% from CQ4 2019 (67.8 M units in CQ4 2019 compared to 77.8 M units in CQ4 2019) compared with down 5.5% in CQ4 2019 from CQ3 2019, up 5.8% in CQ3 from CQ2, up 1.0% in CQ2 2019 from CQ1 2019 and down 11.4% in CQ1 2019 versus CQ4 2018. 

Notebook HDD shipments were down 19.5% from the prior quarter while desktop HDD shipments declined by 27.0% Q2Q.  CE HDD shipments were down 16.2% while branded shipments were down 32.2% Q2Q.  High performance enterprise HDDs were down 10.3% while near line enterprise HDDs were up 26.3% Q2Q (largely due to increased strength in mass storage for data centers to support remote cloud-based work during the COVID-19 pandemic.  

3.5-inch HDDs declined by 9.1% Q/Q.  2.5-inch HDDs decreased by 17.2% Q2Q.   

In Table 1 we see an 8.9% average sales price (ASP) increase from CQ4 2019 to CQ1 2020 compared to an 2.4% ASP increase from CQ3 2019 to CQ4 2019, 4.5% ASP increase from CQ2 2019 to CQ3 2019, a 4.2% increase from CQ1 2019 to CQ2 2019 and a 1.6% increase from CQ4 2018 to CQ1 2019.

Figure 3 shows high, median and low estimate of total drive unit volume estimates out to 2025.   Depending upon results for the balance of 2020, we may reduced our expectations for 2021 and subsequent years.

Figure 4 gives our estimates for HDDs, magnetic media (disks) and heads production out to 2025 based upon the median estimate for HDDs in Figure 3.   The growth of capacity-oriented Near Line drives for enterprise and hyperscale applications will result in more components per drive out to 2025.  We project that total shipments of heads and media will exceed the peak in 2014 by 2021-2022, largely due to the growth of high capacity (many heads and media) hard disk drives.

FIGURE 4.  PROJECTED DEMAND FOR HDD HEADS AND DISKS

Figure 5 shows laboratory demonstrations and product announcement maximum areal densities (information stored per square inch of disk surface) history. 

Figure 6 shows the product announcement maximum areal density per quarter compared to lines representing areal density growth.  Note that have been in a period of extended product and laboratory areal density stagnation, similar to the period from 2011 through 2015.

Figure 7 gives our projections for drives by market niche out to 2025.  Figure 8 does the same for drive form factor.   Note the growth in 3.5 inch form factor HDDs, driven mainly by the growth in Near Line HDDs.

Figure 9 projects total shipments of HDD storage capacity on an annual basis to 2025.  Figure 10 shows the average $/GB for HDDs.  Figure 11 shows total projected shipments for Tape (LTO), SSDs and HDDs.

Growth in HDD shipments is being driven by their use for second tier storage in enterprise and especially data center (cloud) applications.  This is increasing the proportion of 3.5 inch HDDs and also increasing requirements for heads and media for these HDDs.  HDD use in data centers gives the industry a growth opportunity in 2020 to support remote work.

As we head deeper into spring, temperatures are rising—but prices are dropping. Retailers across all categories are marking down some of their most popular items to make way for new designs. So whether you’re looking to revamp your backyard with a new set of outdoor furniture or invest in some new activewear, you’re sure to find what you’re looking for at a serious discount this weekend.

If you’re in the mood to shop for some spring fashion, be sure to shop the current sales at Nordstrom, Levi’s and Macy’s. You’ll find deals for the whole family at all three. Looking for athleisure in particular? Check out Anthropologie, which is currently offering 30% off select activewear and accessories.

On the beauty front, your best bet for finding great markdowns is at Ulta Beauty’s 21 Days of Beauty Sale, where you can shop select items at 50% off. Nordstrom’s Spring Sale also includes popular skincare and makeup products at 15% off, and the Kiehl’s Friends & Family Sale offers 25% off site-wide. The Macy’s VIP Sale also has an impressive beauty section.

If it’s furniture and home decor you’re after, check out this weekend’s sales at Wayfair, Serena & Lily and Overstock. And last but not least, there are some big savings to be had in the tech department as well, from deals on laptops at HP and Samsung to TVs on sale at Walmart. Shop all of these sales and more below, and be sure to check back next week for an updated list of sales.
